subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: James Doe <james.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology

Thanks again for the deep dive earlier today — great conversation. Below is a short recap of the pain, goals, and the proposed next steps so we have alignment before the POC kickoff. I attached a short SLO proposal and a high-level topology diagram for the team.

1) Key pain points you called out
- Tail latency on real-time recommendations spikes during peak traffic windows (especially with 512-token contexts).
- Unpredictable unit cost due to cold starts and suboptimal batching across models.
- Need for strict data isolation and audit logs for compliance.

2) Goals we agreed on
- P95 latency target: 150ms for 512-token generation (95th percentile, production traffic profile).
- Sustained throughput: ~300 reqs/sec at peak for the recommendation route.
- Deployment must be in your VPC (us-west2) and SOC 2-compatible audit trails.

3) Model & infra requirements discussed
- Model: prefer a 70B-class open model (you mentioned Llama2-70B/70B-chat) with int8/4 quantized profile.
- Warm vs cold starts: we recommend pre-warmed pools + KV cache pinning for sessionized flows to keep P95 low.
- Hardware: target H100 class for P95 goals at 512 tokens; A100 is possible with more aggressive batching/quantization but will increase cold-start tail.

4) Proposed deployment topology (high level)
- Dedicated GPU pool in your VPC (two availability zones) with autoscale thresholds based on queue length and token-rate.
- Fast path: quantized 70B model pinned to pre-warmed workers with persistent KV cache per session.
- Fallback: smaller 13B/7B variant or hosted multi-tenant endpoint if capacity constrained.

5) Short-term POC scope & success criteria
- Deploy a dedicated pool to serve the recommendation route for a 48-hour soak.
- Measure P50/P95/P99 latencies, token/sec, and cost per 1k tokens.
- Success if P95 <= 200ms and throughput >= 250 reqs/sec with steady tail behavior.

6) Next steps
- I attached a 1-page SLO proposal and topology diagram (redwood-slo-proposal.pdf, network-topology-diagram.png).
- Proposed POC kickoff: Wed, Mar 11 at 10:00am PT (please confirm).
- I'll loop in our Solutions Engineer to produce initial infra sizing and a runbook.

If I missed anything, flag it and I can update. Thanks — looking forward to getting the POC scheduled.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

Thanks James — great questions. Quick answers below plus an updated ask for the POC plan.

- H100 vs A100 (ballpark):
  - H100: expect P95 ~120-160ms for 512-token generation under quantized 70B with pre-warmed pool and KV cache.
  - A100: expect P95 ~180-260ms for same profile unless we increase batch sizes and rely more on async batching (which can add 10–30ms variability).
  - Recommendation: start with A100 if H100s are not available; configure more pre-warmed workers and conservative autoscale thresholds. We can provide infra sizing guidance for both.

- Cold starts:
  - Cold-first-request P95 can be 1.2–2.5x steady-state depending on model size and container spin-up (we mitigate this with pre-warmed workers and model hot-restarts).
  - For the POC, we'll recommend keeping a minimum pool that covers 20–30% of expected peak concurrent sessions to avoid most cold-starts.

- Security/KMS:
  - We support GCP KMS integration for envelope keys and can emit per-request audit logs to your logging endpoint (we'll work with Lina on log sinks and retention).

POC kickoff ask:
- Wed, Mar 11 at 10:00am PT (we'll schedule a 45-min kickoff with infra + solutions).
- Deliverables: sizing doc, runbook for peering/KMS, and a short smoke test harness for load generation.

Markus (cc) — can you prepare a 1-page sizing note for both H100/A100 by EOD Mon so we can pick a starting footprint?

I'll attach the topology diagram and SLO doc to the calendar invite.
\Best,
Marissa
